definition: Career planning is the ongoing process of developing clear plans for one’s future career. In this source, having clearer career plans is linked with stronger self-efficacy and greater effort toward reaching those plans.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define career planning as “the ongoing process of developing clear plans for one’s future career”; it discusses “the process of career planning” mainly in relation to reinforcement of self-efficacy, without stating the general definition in that wording.

The claim that clearer career plans are linked with “greater effort toward reaching those plans” is only partially supported indirectly (“greater investment required to achieve those plans”); this does not cleanly and directly support the specific phrasing about “greater effort,” so the definition is not fully supported as written.

The packet supports that clearer career plans are associated with higher self-efficacy and greater investment toward achieving those plans, but it does not directly define career planning as an ongoing process of developing clear plans for one’s future career.
The wording slightly overstates the source by turning an association into a general definitional claim about the term itself.
